case.case_title: Wimal Vidyamani v. Lt. Col. Jayatilleke and Others
case.source_citation: Sri Lanka Law Reports [1993] 2 Sri L.R.

clause.text: No person shall be arrested except according to law and must be informed of the reason.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioner was lawfully arrested and detained in accordance with Article 13(1) of the Constitution.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed he was unlawfully arrested without being informed of the reason, detained illegally, and subjected to torture, violating his fundamental rights under Article 13(1).
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents alleged the petitioner had links with the JVP and was involved in subversive attacks, justifying his arrest and detention under emergency regulations.
key_facts: Petitioner was arrested on 19.10.90 by police without being informed of the reason.
Petitioner had an exemplary service record and no material evidence linked him to subversive activities.
Detention orders under emergency regulations were issued but lacked adequate supporting material.
Petitioner was subjected to torture while in police custody.
The Secretary to the Ministry of State for Defence failed to produce material justifying detention.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The Court held that under Article 13(1), arrest must be lawful and the person arrested must be informed of the reason. The validity of arrest under Regulation 18(1) requires an objective test based on adequate material. Detention orders under Regulation 17(1) require a reasonable opinion by the Secretary supported by relevant grounds.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The Court found no material to justify suspicion against the petitioner or to support the detention orders. The petitioner was not informed of the reason for arrest, and the detention orders were mechanically made without proper grounds. Therefore, the arrest and detention violated Article 13(1).
principles_established: Arrest must be according to law and the arrested person must be informed of the reason.
Validity of arrest under emergency regulations requires objective material.
Detention orders require reasonable grounds and cannot be mechanical.
Failure to produce material to justify detention renders arrest and detention unlawful.
precedents_cited: Wickremabandu v. Herat and others [1990] 2 Sri LR. 348
Nanayakkara v. Henry Perera [1985] 2 Sri L.R. 375
Sasanasiritissa Thero v. P. A. de Silva [1989] 2 Sri LR. 356

outcome.holding: The Court held that the petitioner's arrest and detention were unlawful and violated his rights under Article 13(1).
outcome.remedy_or_orders: Declaration of infringement of rights under Article 13(1) and compensation of Rs. 15,000.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 13(1) was central to the Court's determination that the petitioner was unlawfully arrested without being informed of the reason, making the arrest and detention unconstitutional.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The Court found no material to warrant suspicion against the petitioner and held that the arrest under Regulation 18(1) was unlawful. The petitioner was not informed of the reason for arrest and detention orders were mechanically made without proper grounds.
